tagline.text: A beginner-friendly dawn hike in Tanay known for its palm-shaped lookouts and sea of clouds

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May dry season (sea of clouds is best seen at dawn in March–June)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Day trip (6–9 hours starting at dawn)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱560–1,000 per person (day hike from Manila)

children.text: Mount Mapalad is a mountain of roughly 700 meters in Barangay San Andres, Tanay, Rizal, famous for its palm-shaped wooden lookouts (Palad) and dawn sea of clouds. It is a beginner-level hike that can be done in a single day from Manila.

Mount Mapalad rises in Barangay San Andres in Tanay, Rizal, east of Manila. Hiking guides list its height in the high 700-meter range and rate it about 3 out of 9 in difficulty, making it an easy-to-moderate route. You can leave Manila before dawn, catch the sunrise, come down around lunchtime and be back before evening, which is why office workers and Korean families who want to make the most of a weekend day like it.
What made the mountain famous are the Bali-style, palm-shaped wooden structures near the summit. Locals call them
Palad

, the Filipino word for palm of the hand. One is known as the group-photo spot and the other as the solo-photo spot, and the wide Sierra Madre range and sea of clouds behind them have made the place popular on social media. The flip side is long photo queues; on weekends the wait for your turn can take as long as the hike itself.

The trail passes through the village, rice paddies and streams, then forest paths, steep climbs, grassy meadows and a bamboo grove. Much of it has little shade, so it gets quite hot after sunrise. That is why most hikers start around 3–4 AM, greet the sunrise at the top and head down before the sun gets high. A guide is mandatory according to the registration office, and you must pay a registration and environmental fee, so even independent hikers must follow the local procedure. The early flat and stream sections are dark, so watch your footing, and on the climbs after the midpoint keep a steady breath and take your time. Near the top the wind cools you down, so it helps to pack a thin jacket.

The prices and times in this guide are collected from travel blogs and map-service reviews and change over time. Please check current fees and rules with the registration office or your guide before you go.
Near the summit stand two Bali-style palm-shaped wooden structures. The first is known for group photos and the second for solo photos, and each party is often limited to about
5–10 minutes
. Many people come just for this one photo, which makes it the biggest attraction.

blocks.title: Dawn sunrise and sea of clouds

children.text: From the lookout you can watch the sun rise over the Sierra Madre range. The sea of clouds depends on weather and season and is said to be easier to see at dawn in
March–June
. On some days the clouds sit too far away to see, so treat the clouds as a bonus.

blocks.title: The early path across paddies and streams

children.text: For about
30–45 minutes
after the start, the path is a relatively easy mix of flat ground, paddy dikes and stream crossings. It is a good warm-up, and at dawn you can enjoy the quiet atmosphere of a country village.
After the rest hut at the midpoint comes a steep climb of about
2 km
. Reviews call it the hardest part. Some sections have ropes and bamboo handholds, so beginners can get through if they go slowly.
From the lookout to the summit is about
1 km
. You cross a grassy ridge of about
, a bamboo grove and some rocky sections, and the scenery keeps changing.
One guide describes the route past Kinabuan Falls as faster but tougher. It has slippery rock and a steep slope, so take care after rain and ask your guide which route is usable that day.

It is close to Manila and can be done in a day, and a guide leads the way, so even people with little hiking experience can try it. Some travelers combine it with other Rizal attractions such as Masungi or Daraitan on a longer trip.

children.text: Leave Manila. According to one guide, if you are not going for the sunrise you can leave around
Finish registration and guide assignment and set off. The sun is strong at this hour, so bring a hat and umbrella.
Reach the area near the summit and enjoy the view and photos. The photo queue may be long on weekends.
Descend and have lunch and a rest at the registration office. Leave for Manila before dark.
With so little shade, a midday hike is tiring. For the sunrise and sea of clouds, a dawn hike is better.

items.title: From Manila by car or van

children.text: From Manila take Marcos Highway through Cogeo in Antipolo to Barangay San Andres. It is said to take about
1–2 hours
depending on traffic.
For five or more people, renting a van or a car is more convenient. One review reported a van from Cubao for six people at

Search for Mt. Mapalad on Google Maps to find the location. Roads are quiet at dawn, but the local road is dark and narrow, so drive slowly.

In Cogeo, transfer to a jeepney bound for San Andres, get off in Barangay San Andres and tell the driver you are going to Mt. Mapalad or the Mt. Batolusong jump-off. Cogeo to San Andres was reported in 2019 at about
From San Andres, take a tricycle to the registration office. The last trip is said to be around

For a sunrise hike, the first public transport runs too late to make it. That is why many people share a van or join a tour.
Another route is to take a jeepney from Tanay Public Market toward Sampaloc, then transfer at the junction to a jeepney toward Cogeo and get off at San Andres.
Travelers who want to combine the hike with Tanay Old Town sometimes use this route.

The best time to visit Mount Mapalad is the dry season. In the rainy season the trail turns to slippery mud and streams can swell and become dangerous to cross. After heavy rain the rock sections are especially slippery, so follow your guide's judgment.

According to one guide, the sea of clouds is best seen at dawn in March–June. It varies by day, however, so check the forecast and cloud conditions and keep your expectations modest. Weekends and holidays are very crowded, and on weekdays the photo queue is much shorter.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Dawn can be chilly, so a thin jacket helps. It is peak season, so weekends are crowded.
A sea of clouds is possible but midday is very hot. A dawn start and plenty of water are essential.
Rainy season, frequent rain and clouds
Mud and swollen streams are a risk and you may miss the sunrise. Avoid rainy days.

Around the registration office in San Andres there are shower facilities and you can get simple meals. Reviews say it is hard to buy food or water up the mountain, so prepare snacks and water in advance. In one review the hikers had lunch and rested at the registration office after descending.

For lodging you can camp or use a hotel in Tanay or Antipolo. Tent rental at the registration office is reported if you have no tent, but this varies, so ask in advance. If sunrise is your goal, you could also stay in Antipolo the night before and travel in the early morning.

Wear quick-drying clothes and closed shoes with non-slip soles. Some people are said to climb in slippers or sandals, but feet are easily hurt on rocks and in mud. After a midday descent you will be sweaty, so leave a change of clothes and a towel in your vehicle and freshen up at the registration office showers before heading back. Most places take cash only, so bring plenty of small bills.
For a dawn hike, be sure to bring a headlamp and spare batteries.
Bring at least
2 liters
of water. Many reviews said there are almost no stalls midway up.
Everyone in your group must stand in the photo queue in person, and guides reportedly cannot hold a place for you. Ask your guide when the queue is shortest.
The wait can be long, so a picnic mat, umbrella and snacks make it more comfortable.
Muddy and slippery rock sections are common, so wear hiking shoes or similar footwear with good grip.
Put valuables and electronics in a waterproof bag. Rain can arrive suddenly.
Avoid weekends; going on a weekday is much more relaxed.
Carry out all your trash and do not write on trees or rocks.
If you wait a long time at the lookout your body can cool down, so keep a thin jacket in your bag.
After rain the rocks and mud are very slippery and streams can rise, so let your guide decide whether to hike.
There is little shade in many places, so heatstroke is a risk in daytime. Bring a hat and plenty of water.
You can fall on slippery rock and steep slopes. Hold the ropes and handholds and move one person at a time.
Always stay with your guide so you do not get lost on the dark dawn trail.
Fees and guide rules can change, so check the latest announcements.
Do not cut in line at the weekend photo queue; wait your turn.
A conservation-area experience route in the same province of Rizal. It has advance booking and rules, so check the official website and plan it as a separate outing.
The best-known waterfall in the Tanay area, where many hikers stop to cool off after the climb. Travel time depends on traffic.

blocks.title: Tanay Old Town and San Ildefonso Church

children.text: The center of Tanay, with historic buildings such as San Ildefonso Church. It connects with the public transport route through the market.
Another popular hiking destination in Rizal. It is best planned as a separate day trip.
